key_insight: PIKS extends kernel learning to physics-informed problems and proves it can converge to the true solution while enforcing linear differential constraints, even without assuming the target lies in the RKHS.
engineering_relevance: This offers a mathematically tractable surrogate modeling option for solid mechanics and FEM-style physics problems where PINNs are harder to analyze and kernel methods are usually too restrictive.
method: Use a universal kernel (e.g., Gaussian or Matérn) with physics constraints encoded through differential operators.
Analyze the estimator with operator-theoretic kernel learning tools to prove universal consistency.
Derive finite-sample error bounds under source conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing PIKS can be competitive with PINNs and traditional finite element methods.
watch_item: Performance and guarantees depend on linear constraints and suitable source conditions, so extension to more complex nonlinear physics may require additional care.
